featured_reviews.name: Ginny
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited the Passport Seva Kendra at Andheri East, Mumbai today for my passport renewal, and overall it was a smooth experience.

My appointment was at 10:30AM. I reached at 9:45 AM and was completely done by 10:45 AM — very efficient!

The entire process at Passport Seva Kendra Andheri East was well managed:

• Counter A – Photograph & biometrics (quick and smooth)• Counter B – Document verification (fastest process)• Counter C – Final approval and stamping (also very quick)

Movement between counters A, B, and C was seamless. Staff at most counters were professional and efficient. The security guard was polite and helpful.

The only downside was the lady issuing tokens at Counter 2 (wearing glasses). She was quite rude and could definitely improve her communication. Maybe she was overworked, but basic courtesy goes a long way.

Another suggestion: the toilets need better maintenance. Having a dedicated cleaner stationed there would improve hygiene standards significantly.

For anyone going for renewal  without any changes, it’s not complicated at all. I carried:

Voter ID

PAN Card

Aadhaar (A4 printed version with verified signature, not just the smart card)

Original passport + photocopies of first and last two pages
All self attested..
They only asked me for the Voter ID & my passport during the process. No one asked for DigiLocker or any digital documents.

Overall, apart from one staff interaction and the restroom cleanliness, it was a very good and efficient experience.
All officers were kind n helpful .Thank you

The entire process was seamless and very professionally managed. Moving from counter A to B to C was like a breeze. The staff at all counters were professional, efficient and very helpful. In flat 20 minutes, the work was completed and I was out.
To my utmost surprise, I got the delivery of my new passport on the 3rd day, today, 9th May (though regular, and not Tatkal).
I am very impressed by the entire process and wish to congratulate our Indian Govt for this express service.
Jai Hind.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Rating as of 15/4/26.
1 star reduced due to C1 counter lady officer attitude towards applicants. She doesn't have manners to talk with people, big thumbs down for her👎.
4 stars only for security guards, receiptionst, Counter A, B and C3 officer (MR. Korlekar) even exit counter security, big thumbs up 👍
Overall experience was good not great. It could have been great.

Applied for normal passport for myself and for 2 kids. .

• At the entry security guard checks appointment letter or mobile copy and allow inside only who's appointment is.
• At security check post which is inside building, 2 guards verify appointment letter, all xerox copies along with original and allow only applicants inside.
• At reception they verify all the documents xerox set, original and ask to get token from scanner machine, which is nearby. Don't expect kindness here from reception executives as rush might kill their sympathy. You will get token from reception.
• Note: there are three counters A, B and C, each counter has different checks.
• You need to enter into counter A ZONE. At Counter A, they asks us to verify application form on monitor. They click photograph from their DSLR, you can see your clicked photo live. Finger scanner done later, sign on each xerox copies. Show original here as well. Then they pull us to B counter.
• You have to go at B counter ZONE. There are multiple subcounters are there B1, B2, B3, B4. Your token number and B sub counter will display on screen, wait for your for your turn. At B counters again all copies are checked. But key point here is they ask for digilocker and link Adhar with it. Then they route you to last counter i.e. C.
• After B counter verification you have to wait in the same B counter zone and wait for your token and C sub counter to be displayed on same screen.
• Once your token code and C sub counter displays on screen, you have to walk a way at C counter ZONE. Note, in C counter ZONE there are 4 subcounters C1, C2, C3, C3 are there, your token code and C sub counter will display.
• At C subcounters, it is one of the fastest process as compared to A and B. Here they closely look at your application print, xerox copies and all original. Then they grant application in the system. Note, stamp is not required for fresh passport application. You have to walk towards exist door which is on the right side.
• After C counter ZONE verification are done. You will get SMS and email about your application process, tracking ID and police verification.

There was zero ownership of their mistake, no apology, and no urgency—just endless follow-ups from my side.

This company thrives on false timelines, poor accountability, lost paperwork, and last-minute money demands, knowing that customers are helpless once their documents are stuck in the system. It feels like a deliberate strategy rather than an accident.

ITseazy wasted three months of my time, caused immense stress, and showed complete contempt for customer trust. I am initiating legal action through the consumer court and will ensure my experience is publicly documented on every review platform possible so others are not fooled by their marketing.

If you are considering ITseazy, understand this clearly:
They take your money first, delay endlessly, lose documents, and then ask for more money.

Avoid this company at all costs unless you enjoy being ignored, misled, and financially squeezed.

featured_reviews.name: Paritosh Shiledar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Passport Seva Kendra Malad– Detailed Experience Review

Appointment & Arrival
My reporting time was 9:15 AM and appointment time 9:30 AM. I reached the location around 8:30 AM, which helped a lot since there were only two people ahead of me.

---

Location & Accessibility

The centre is located in a busy market area with street vendors and vegetable sellers near the entrance, so the surroundings feel crowded. However, accessibility is good and the location is not far from the Western Express Highway.

---

Parking

Parking is available for passport applicants in the basement of an adjacent building. I was able to park my car easily, probably because I arrived early. Security guards near the parking area are helpful, though they do tend to ask for tips (I ended up giving ₹20 each). Capacity for parking is unclear, so early arrival is advisable.

---

Process & Timeline

The overall process is systematic but involves multiple steps:

1. Entry & Photocopy Counter
Since I arrived early, I was allowed inside earlier than my reporting time. The first step was a photocopy counter where I had to buy a ₹4 Tatkal undertaking form.

2. Token Counter
Documents and originals were checked, and a token was issued.

3. Counter A
Documents were scanned and uploaded, and the photograph was taken. Once uploaded, documents become accessible across Counters A, B, and C.
Staff here (likely privately recruited) were professional and polite.

4. Waiting Area → Counter B
After Counter A, applicants wait until their token appears on the screen. Counter B mainly verifies originals; in my case, very little interaction happened. The govt employee should have checked my originals. He just let me go to Counter C where queries were raised

5. Counter C (Final Approval)
This is the final approval stage handled by a gazetted officer.

---

Staff Experience

Counter A staff were professional and courteous.
Staff at Counters B and C (government employees) were noticeably less polite and less helpful. Interaction felt rigid and somewhat dismissive.

One important observation: despite alternative documents being listed on the passport website, acceptance seemed to depend heavily on officer discretion.

In my case:

I had a registered rent agreement as address proof.
The officer demanded a bank passbook as photo ID, which I had not carried.
My company photo ID (from a public listed company), although listed as acceptable online, was rejected.
Digilocker documents were also not accepted despite broader government policy supporting them and paperless bharat.

This makes the experience feel unpredictable and somewhat dependent on individual officers.

---

Overall Experience

The process was quick — I finished and exited by around 9:45 AM, which is impressive timing. However, I had to go back and forth between counters due to document preferences and verification issues.

**Pros**

* Fast processing when slots are less crowded
* Parking availability
* Organized digital workflow at Counter A

**Cons**

* Crowded surrounding area
* Informal expectation of tips near parking
* Inconsistent document acceptance
* Mixed professionalism across counters

All the best

If you're dreaming of exploring South Africa, you absolutely need to check out Passport Paradise. They've nailed the perfect mix of luxury and authentic local experiences. I'm already planning my next trip with them ! 🦁✨
